title: The Year He Does Not Count

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A slate counts what a house is owed. A man counts what he owes the house. The two counts never meet, and the year between them is the one he cannot spend.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the clay-bound, Low Kiln

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-seven-to-one-hundred-and-nine-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the held breath read as a breath held against a clamp, the order of reaching for the record before the person, the watcher's delay filed as an object after the knock, the exact count kept against a house that keeps its days in loaves and glances) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room or collector interior

scenes.title: At the Edge of the Sill
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 107, Seed 18, Eighthday, before first grey through midday at the yard well and in the Clay Yard; going of the light under the Vail roof. Tarn's seventh year stands at the very edge of the sill and is still held: the small bench knife lies on its sill with six years in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house cannot check, and to the kindling he says Six counted. The next I don't count. His chest has been tight since the dark and the breath is still unspent; he takes the broom only after Sella Vail has given it its instruction, goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector over and over without once turning along it, and keeps the unforged sentence from the frozen ford where he keeps the seventh year, entering neither. The planting goes on under the same arithmetic: hands in the worked strips east of Low Kiln counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called and the sentence that would call it is still unsaid under this roof. Something must give at the end of the seventh year; it does not give here. The boy, carried at the edge, reads the held breath as a breath held against a clamp --- exact, worth nothing --- and keeps one hundred and seven exact against a house that keeps its days badly. Advances T036/T076, T071/T072 (107), T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082. Withheld: no seventh year spent, no collector sentence entered, no turn along the road, no ending.

scenes.title: The Date Over the Sign
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 107, Seed 18, midday three doors down in House Silt and afternoon at the loaf shelf under the Vail roof. Sella sets the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door at the edge of the light away from every open slate, opens no slate and turns no errand into a walk to Slate Row. Alda Reed lays her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turns to the fold, presses the wool a breath too long, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows it and covers the sign with the date she gave Dessa, says Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down, exact and not true, and goes on with dates after the question has stopped. Her hand goes once into her bodice to the little tin and comes away without opening it; the sixth narrow slate stays face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy cannot name, six pages in a second hand all unread, no seventh written and T023 not paid again. Above the abandoned board-bed the round pewter tin keeps its pale fold and thumb-bright rub unopened while the grey wool below holds only the hollow where the small pale river stone lay, and nobody says either is gone. At the loaf shelf a neighbour reaches past the bare board and calls the old space a thing the planting brought in, her hand to the board before her eyes to the boy, and goes off with her pot without seeing the empty place at his ear; the boy files the saying beside the one already waiting there, T097 advanced and not paid, and keeps the shelf's two unnamed gaps in one room from touching the fold's one stiff crust and its unnamed empty place in another. Sella gives nobody a figure, glances at the clay jar, touches the widow's mark at no hour because a shelf and a bed are not openings, and tells the fire it is the thaw; the fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seven days. Advances T023/T089, T007/T008/T073, T060/T086, T097 (advanced, not paid), T058/T079, T088, T009/T013/T092, T061/T082, T071/T072 (107). Withheld: no tin opened, no seventh note, no name or number from Dessa, no joining of the two rooms, no third gap.

scenes.title: The Wheel Before the Hands
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 108, Seed 19, Ninthday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, and the Clay Yard. Men have come in before first grey and spoken low in the back room and Jorra Vail gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold. He comes through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel, and the boy keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray without asking which slate was broken or whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody. Jorra speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot You'll do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln who would call it early and make something of it. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence, the iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted; he has not answered with a word and has not looked at her. The boy reads the iron once more as the bite that holds a vessel whole and can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, and files it as an object joined to no kiln. The promise of the foundling's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn. Advances T035/T031, T062, T076/T036, T058/T079, T061/T082, T071/T072 (108). Withheld: no name for the men, no opening of the back room, no birth-slate examined, no seventh hearing, no name given.

scenes.title: The Watcher's Turn
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 108, Seed 19, dawn market below the north bridge at the Fishstairs; going of the light under the Vail roof. Sella sets the basket at the end of the fish-trade shade where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the water and never to the basket. Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves and silt dried pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little to the right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, and moves eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays, and shifting a creel shows the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched; her board lies beside Orra Weir's knot-string and does not touch it. At the market's edge a foundling in cast-off clothes worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in the creases of his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead-glaze on a string at his throat, is glimpsed unnamed and silent: when a pot is set down his head goes toward it a half-beat after the boy's, after the knuckle and after the note, then stops, and he rubs the sliver and cannot say why. No loaf passes, no slate is seen, no sentence finished for a kiln-hand, no secret sold. The boy sets the watcher's turning beside the two tellings of the shelf without joining any of them. The steps come back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walks over carefully without a fall; the soft-cuffed clerk still sits with his cuff grey from washing and his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector and the Court-table clerk, with no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand. Advances T033/T034, T059/T025/T024, T090/T080, T083, T097 (advanced, not paid), T071/T072 (108), T058/T079. Withheld: no knot counted, no word forty, no sixth sighting, no sale, no betrayal paid, no dialogue for the watcher.

scenes.title: One in Twelve, As the Notice Says
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 109, Seed 20, Tenthday, Account-day, morning at the Cross reading block and the worked strips beyond; the boy carried at the half-pace from every open slate and set in the moot-post's shade. Berr Clay comes up with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and green of tasted glaze at one corner of his mouth, hot clay over the smell of nothing at all; his hands are large and clean and he wipes his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing and holds a narrow slate unopened against his forearm, passing a finger over the figure and letting his eyes rest on it a breath longer than the writing required. He reads one in twelve, as the notice says low into the crowd over the worked ground where hands went in on Seed 15, calls the levy and says it is not called by him, and to a man who brings a number up out of a fist and asks what the planting cost now that hands have been in it says a number goes into a slate and not into a strip; if the house wants it again, there'll be a slate at the watch --- your house, never I, taking himself out of his own sentence as neatly as a hand out of a field. The figure read aloud is not the figure paid; the true subtraction goes over the strips unspoken and sits in the locked box in his house up the road, and nothing in the ground changes its figure because a man has looked at it. The bell at the Cross goes four, four and a gap and nobody crosses himself; the soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the Fishstairs for a measure nobody called. Berr never looks into the basket and goes off toward High Kiln believing he has done the district a kindness, Garl's debt against the firing of tiles neither paid nor settled. The boy keeps the heard bell beside the told bell in two places and adds no seventh hearing. Advances T015/T041/T047/T077/T078, T090/T080, T009, T061/T082, T071/T072 (109), T058/T079. Withheld: no true figure, no opening of the box, no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no ending.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Nine
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 109, Seed 20, Account-day, midday through the going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof. Sella carries him home at the half-pace from every open slate, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread of drool at his mouth frozen and unwiped, because nobody has been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left. The boy turns out the private file the way a man turns out instruments on a towel and finds it unchanged: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals on another tray, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn and the weight of a thumb apart, four low things in four places with the river's note of water over water a fifth, the two tellings of the shut counting room joined to no kiln with no third, the damper's double bite filed as an object, and the loan that can hear still uncalled. The one crust in the fold stays stiff with its empty place unnamed and no third; the shelf in the next room keeps two unnamed gaps; below the sill the child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, uncured, uncaused and unnamed. The clean dark line and the new finer grey lie unswept and are called the thaw; the space under the lowest rack is gone around and entered by nobody; no opening came, so the widow's mark hangs untouched and Sella's private roll stays unshown. She tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot and feeds it; the fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and nine days. She says the house where another woman would say I and does not look toward the bed. The door stands a finger's width open: the river's note comes through the gap and the kiln's four, four and a gap through the floor, the two sounds in two separate places; the boards overhead keep four nails and four and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb, and the counts do not meet. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down; the count stands at one hundred and nine, unspent, and the dark under the roof keeps it without a figure. Advances T061/T082, T060/T086, T093/T094/T096, T023/T089, T059/T025/T024, T036/T076, T009/T013/T092, T088, T071/T072 (109), T058/T079. Withheld: no seventh hearing, no joining, no payment, no silt-leach named, no ending --- the planting month goes into its last tend and Day 110 belongs to Chapter 24.
